R7AD-bear-walk-0001.name: By Horse Creek
R7AD-bear-walk-0001.pressureWhy: 3.6 km on foot from the nearest parking (estimate).
R7AD-bear-walk-0001.parkWhat: pull off on E Canoe FSR (gravel road)

evidence.t: Cutblock harvested 2016 (10 years old), 170 m NW: cutblocks and logging road edges green up first in spring (65%) and grow berries for the fall feed (lesson: Black bear).
SE facing slope, 33 degrees: grassy south facing slopes are spring bear food (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
Horse Creek 120 m SE: stream sides and skunk cabbage swamps are spring food, and bears forage on berries and spawning fish in fall (90%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 5).
1 km or more from pavement and 2 km from a town: bears near people feed more at night (75%, lesson: Black bear Masterclass 6).

plan: Drive: from Village of Valemount, about 29 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Whiskeyfill Rd, Bailey Rd, Canoe Rd, E Canoe FSR.
Park: 52.68608, -119.02809, pull off on E Canoe FSR (gravel road). Map links below.
Walk: 3.6 km NE, cross country, no trail mapped. Climb about 689 m, about 142 min at 3 km/h.

Hunt: black bear, Apr, May, June, Aug, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Glass berry slopes, cutblocks and road edges at dawn and the last 2 hours of light, wind in your face (Tip). A bear under 2 years old and any bear with it are closed (99%, synopsis page 11).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 180 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-2, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-07-31, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AD-bear-walk-0001.recName: Horse Creek Recreation Site rec site
R7AD-bear-walk-0001.recDirections: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km, then turn east onto Cedarside Road towards Kinbasket Lake. Continue onto Canoe East Forest Service Road/Canoe River Forest Rd for 20.5km and then turn right onto the short site access road. Caution: may be industrial traffic.
R7AD-bear-walk-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-2: about 179 hunter days a year for black bear (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.05 days per square km, bottom third of BC MUs; access: a long walk from parking. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

R7AD-grouse-atv-0001.name: 550 m SE of Yellowjacket Creek
R7AD-grouse-atv-0001.pressureWhy: No town, pavement or rec site within 1 km and not behind a closure (estimate).
R7AD-grouse-atv-0001.parkWhat: where the truck road ends (E Canoe FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle)

evidence.t: 100% of the stretch in grouse forest zones (BWBS, CWH, ESSF, ICH, IDF, MS, SBPS, SBS).
6 cutblocks touch the road (30 years old or less): edges and clover.
8 wetlands, lakes or creeks along the road: riparian edges.

seasonRows.notes: No row in the Region 7A table (page 57), so no general open season (page 5: open seasons are only those in the synopsis). MU 7-1 is listed in Region 7A on page 2 but no row names it.

plan: Drive: from Village of Valemount, about 27 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Whiskeyfill Rd, Bailey Rd, Canoe Rd, E Canoe FSR.
Park: 52.70462, -119.04428, where the truck road ends (E Canoe FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Walk 3.7 km to the start. Ride: the Yellowjacket Mainline stretch, 4.7 km one way. About 93 min one way at 3 km/h.
Hunt: grouse, Sept, Oct, Nov (season rows). Walk slowly in the first and last 2 hours of light. Watch where cutblocks and creeks meet the road (Tip).
Use: .22 rimfire for a sitting grouse inside 25 m (27 yd), or a shotgun with lead 6 or 7.5 (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 7-2, Region 7A. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-07-31, closures 2026-10-16.
R7AD-grouse-atv-0001.recDirections: From Valemount, proceed south on Yellowhead Highway 5 for 3km, then turn east onto Cedarside Road towards Kinbasket Lake. Continue onto Canoe East Forest Service Road/Canoe River Forest Rd for 18km and then turn right onto the site access road. Caution: may be industrial traffic.
R7AD-grouse-atv-0001.popWhy: Less popular (quieter): MU 7-2: about 3,512 hunter days a year for all big game (2020 to 2024 mean), 1.04 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: average access. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).
